newsitem.title: EGYPT: EGYPT STATE TO PRIVATISE TWO RICE MILLS.
newsitem.headline: EGYPT STATE TO PRIVATISE TWO RICE MILLS.

text.p: Egypt's state-owned Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills on Tuesday offered investors two rice mills in the Dakahliya and Beheira provinces for sale by auction as part of the government's privatisation programme.

It said in a published advertisement the Abu el-Futuh mill in Dakahliya could produce 90 tonnes of white rice a day and the Mahmoudiya mill's daily capacity was 80 tonnes. The deadline for bids for Abu el-Futuh is May 4 and a day later for Mahmoudiya.

The state has sold part of its stake in several flour milling firms over the past 18 months but officials have often said the government will maintain control over the sector because of its "strategic" nature. Egypt subsidises its bread.
Last month, the state said it would also auction investors a rice mill in the Nile Delta province of Mansoura.
The state-owned National Bank of Egypt is handling the sale.
